title: What happened in AI — Nov 24, 2026
intro: Agents got gates today. Google made Workspace MCP servers generally available behind a new Cloud Agent Gateway that checks permissions and asks a human before sensitive actions, and Postgres.ai published a benchmark for whether agent-written SQL is safe on production databases.

The coding-agent evidence is now about verified output: iFood routes work across 15,000+ repos to sandboxed agents that return merge requests, and a new benchmark shows Opus 5 building inference engines that beat vLLM in 71% of runs.
highlights: Google GA's Workspace MCP servers and CLI, plus Cloud Agent Gateway for permission checks and human confirmation.
iFood runs coding agents across 15,000+ repos via remote sandboxes; security fixes more than doubled.
Opus 5 built inference engines from scratch in 12 hours that beat vLLM in 71% of runs.
Google and Mandiant report multi-agent frameworks exploiting vulnerabilities autonomously in live attacks.
Google DeepMind launches Humanity's First Exam to test consistency on everyday questions.
vLLM ships day-0 support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview (280B MoE, 1M context).

categories.name: Coding and web agents: sandboxed runs, verified actions
categories.summary: Today's agent-practice stories replace per-step model judgment with a checkable artifact: a merge request from a remote sandbox, a verified server, or a typed page operation.

articles.title: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
articles.summary: iFood's Remote Agents Platform turns tasks across 15,000+ repos into API calls that run in a remote sandbox and return a merge request; vulnerabilities fixed more than doubled on its security platform.

articles.title: Can agents write inference engines from scratch in 12 hours and beat vLLM?
articles.summary: Long-horizon benchmark asks agents to build an inference engine from scratch in 12 hours; Opus 5's servers passed verification and beat the vLLM baseline in 71% of runs.

articles.title: Compiling web applications into verified operations for AI agents
articles.summary: Protocolis compiles an unseen web page's controls into typed operations with no model inference, then reports what each action actually changed, so the model stops re-reading the page every step.

categories.name: Agent permissions before production writes
categories.summary: Agent access is getting a control plane: permission checks, human confirmation, and safety tests now sit between agents and the systems they change, while attackers already run agents of their own.

articles.title: Built for trust and control: Powering the next wave of AI agents across Google Workspace and Google Cloud
articles.summary: Google makes Workspace MCP servers and the Workspace CLI generally available and adds Cloud Agent Gateway for permission checks, human confirmation of sensitive actions, and prompt screening.

articles.title: PGAIBench and AAA: can AI safely change production Postgres?
articles.summary: Postgres.ai's PGAIBench targets the real blocker for AI database ops: knowing whether agent-written SQL is safe to run on a live production cluster, toward one DBRE overseeing 1,000 clusters.

articles.title: Google has uncovered an autonomous AI cyber attack
articles.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report attackers using multi-agent frameworks that find and exploit vulnerabilities on their own, already in live campaigns.

categories.name: Evals: consistency and judge bias
categories.summary: Two eval releases target failure modes capability leaderboards miss: whether a model answers simple questions the same way every time, and whether an LLM judge favors its own family.

articles.title: Humanity's First Exam: Testing LLM Reliability
articles.summary: Google DeepMind's Humanity's First Exam on Kaggle measures whether models answer straightforward everyday questions consistently, not whether they can solve a hard task once.

articles.title: Can an LLM Grade Objective Facts Without Favoring Itself?
articles.summary: Tests whether reference-based grading (verbatim source quote, answer key, anonymized IDs) removes LLM-judge self-preference, on a 123-question closed-book testbed.

categories.name: Data context agents can read
categories.summary: Databricks pushes the same point from two sides: an agent's decision is only as good as the governed business context it can reach.

articles.title: Sharing catalog metadata across data platforms, engines, and agents
articles.summary: Catalog labels in the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API expose business purpose, ownership, and data classification to any compatible engine or agent, not just one platform.

articles.title: Data Modeling Best Practices for an Agentic CDP, Part 1: The Data Foundation
articles.summary: Part 1 of an agentic CDP data-modeling series: a single price-drop alert needs answers from six kinds of customer data before an agent can decide.

categories.name: Inference serving and new open-weight models
categories.summary: vLLM ships day-0 support for a 280B MoE and a serving framework for recommendation models, while Zhipu's GLM-5.4 arrives with only secondhand reports.

articles.title: vLLM Day-0 Support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview: Plugin Deployment and E2E Inference Acceleration
articles.summary: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview (280B total, 14B active MoE, 1M-token context, tool calling) runs on release day via a vLLM-ERNIE plugin installed beside the vllm==0.32.0 wheel.

articles.title: Announcing vLLM-GR: Efficient Inference for Generative Recommendation
articles.summary: vLLM-GR extends vLLM's paged KV cache with beam search so generative recommendation models such as OneRec can explore multiple candidate item IDs in one request.

articles.title: Zhipu launches GLM-5.4: 750B base model delivers 2-3T-class performance, Loop architecture debuts in a flagship model
articles.summary: Press reports say Zhipu's GLM-5.4 uses a 750B base model with a Loop architecture and claims 2–3T-class performance; no first-party benchmarks or pricing in today's coverage.
